note: Three gap types (Fresco). A Discovery Gap is NOT 'run another experiment' — the data exists but cannot distinguish the competing hypotheses; what is missing is observation DEPTH. The ladder is ordered shallow→deep (low→high cost): the system asks for the SHALLOWEST depth that would discriminate, not a full battery.

discovery_gap.when: data exists but does not distinguish competing hypotheses

depth_ladder.reveals: how it failed (crack / blister / delamination / gelation)

worked_example.reason: current observations cannot distinguish H1 from H2
worked_example.note: shallowest depth that discriminates — no SEM/FTIR needed yet

discriminability_link: A Discovery Gap is formally a Discriminating Evidence Gap (config/discriminability_v1.json, lib/discriminability.js). The suggested_depth is NOT inferred by the system — it is the human-declared discriminator (distinguished_by) that is missing from the Evidence Set, surfaced at the shallowest cost. The system checks declared discriminators; it never decides what discriminates.
